strengths: Addresses an important practical question: whether low-variance pathwise policy gradients can be made effective in massively parallel, replay-free continuous-control learning.
The evaluation is broad, covering 23 MuJoCo Playground tasks and 8 ManiSkill tasks. It reports per-task curves, aggregate robust statistics, confidence intervals, and ten seeds for REPPO.
The paper evaluates several practically relevant dimensions beyond final return, including sample efficiency, training stability, wall-clock time, replay-buffer size, and architectural ablations.
The empirical results against PPO are often strong, and the comparison with full- and restricted-buffer FastTD3 provides useful evidence that on-policy pathwise learning can be competitive.
weaknesses: The central algorithm is not specified consistently enough to establish technical soundness or permit faithful reproduction. Equation 13 gives an invalid normalization for the finite TD(lambda) return; Equation 19 updates the KL multiplier using entropy again; the stated multiplier behavior has the wrong direction for enforcing an upper KL bound; Equation 16 uses KL(new||old), whereas Equation 20 estimates KL(old||new); and Equations 14 and 20 do not match Algorithm 1. The auxiliary loss and entropy-target indexing also differ between the pseudocode and prose.

The paper does not isolate its main causal claim. There is no matched score-function variant using the same critic, regularization, architecture, and optimization budget; nor are critic accuracy, gradient bias/variance, or gradient alignment measured. Consequently, the advantage over PPO cannot confidently be attributed to pathwise gradients.

The claimed novelty is largely an integration of established components: TD(lambda), maximum-entropy learning, KL-constrained updates, HL-Gauss, layer normalization, and self-prediction. Directly relevant alternatives such as SVG-style on-policy pathwise learning and V-MPO are not experimentally compared, and the characterization of V-MPO as off-policy is questionable.

The ablations omit the most distinctive claim: joint adaptive entropy and KL tuning. There are no comparisons against fixed multipliers, entropy-only or KL-only tuning, the two KL directions, or the proposed clipped variant. Hyperparameter robustness is also asserted without sensitivity studies, while gamma and the critic support are adjusted per environment.

Experimental reporting contains consequential ambiguities. The default configuration states 50 million steps, but several main and appendix curves extend to 200 million; baseline seed counts and tuning budgets differ; some baselines are imported from prior implementations; and the hindsight-based reliability metric depends on an arbitrary 0.9 threshold without sufficient evaluation-protocol details.

The memory evidence measures numbers of stored transitions rather than peak bytes, despite REPPO and FastTD3 storing different fields. The wall-clock comparison is limited to JAX PPO on one benchmark and hardware setting, so the broad efficiency claims are stronger than the evidence.

Reproducibility is presently inadequate: the promised code address is blank, the experimental section contains an unresolved “??” reference, crucial architecture details are deferred to the unavailable codebase, and Table 1 gives identical formulas for vmin and vmax. Policy parameterization, evaluation details, tuning budgets, and ablation seed counts are also missing.
